questions.text: How does a standard Vision Transformer convert an image into inputs for its transformer encoder?

options.A: It treats each color channel as a single token and discards spatial position.
options.B: It flattens image patches, projects them into embeddings, and adds positional signals.
options.C: It converts pixels into word IDs using a pretrained language tokenizer.
options.D: It replaces each attention head with a convolution over the original image.

questions.explanation: ViT turns non-overlapping flattened patches into learned embedding vectors and supplies positional information before processing the sequence.

questions.text: A 224 × 224 image uses non-overlapping 16 × 16 patches and one prepended [CLS] token. How many tokens enter the encoder?
questions.explanation: There are (224/16) squared = 196 patches, plus one [CLS] token, giving 197 tokens.
The grid has (24/6)*(24/6)=16 patches; each contains 6*6*3=108 channel values.
